extracted.intended_audience: email marketers and content teams at media/publishers (especially satirical/humor outlets)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and operating email newsletters for a satirical publisher, covering subject lines, content curation, frequency, tracking, templates, and brand/voice concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject lines are crucial
rubrics_metrics.description: Just like headlines are a crucial part of any Onion story, good subject lines are essential to their email marketing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat subject lines with high importance; they determine open rates and should be carefully chosen and tested. The Onion agonizes over standard news headlines through a strict approval process; simpler infographic-style headlines often perform better as subject lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial approval process for headlines
rubrics_metrics.description: “Our standard news headlines are agonized over and subject to a strict approval process by our editorial staff.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep headline/subject line selection under editorial control. Use a review/approval workflow to maintain quality and brand voice; prioritize headlines that survive this process for canonical promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer simple, infographic-style subject lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Simpler infographic headlines perform much better as subject lines—IE, ‘Blizzard Survival Tips’ or ‘The Onion’s Guide To Gym Etiquette.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, lead off newsletters with straightforward, list/guide-style subject lines that signal quick value. These can outperform elaborate satirical headlines in inbox contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use prior social performance to select newsletter content
rubrics_metrics.description: Almost all of the content in our newsletters has already been socially promoted, so we already have a strong sense of what we should include based on prior performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include pieces that have shown traction on social channels; leverage existing performance data to predict email engagement and reduce risk when curating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekly newsletters should cherry-pick best-performing content
rubrics_metrics.description: The weekly newsletter is a collection of the best performing content from the previous week. For the weekly campaign, traffic dictates curation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curate weeklies by selecting top-performing items (traffic, shares, clicks) rather than simply recency; emphasize quality over quantity for lower-frequency sends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily newsletter format and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Their daily newsletter is simple—just five stories—and what goes in depends on what’s published and ready to be promoted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep daily sends concise (example: five links/stories) and only promote content that is publish-ready and appropriate for email audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segmentation and targeted one-off campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Product and design teams take advantage of how easy it is to create and house new templates within Mailchimp. It’s made it easier to develop one-offs for more highly targeted marketing emails that go out to various segments of our lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build templates and one-off campaigns to serve distinct audience segments; tailor messaging and content selection to segment interests and behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track open and click-through rates closely
rubrics_metrics.description: Our CMS-based system didn’t allow for easy viewing of open and click-through rates, so we now keep a close eye on those.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use email platform analytics to monitor opens and clicks; let those metrics inform subject-line choices, content selection, timing, and segmentation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary objective: drive traffic (not direct revenue)
rubrics_metrics.description: The main objective for The Onion’s email campaigns is to drive traffic, not make money directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design newsletters to maximize site visits and engagement rather than immediate monetization; advertising can be secondary and experimental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautious approach to newsletter ads/monetization
rubrics_metrics.description: Jordan’s team has dabbled in newsletter advertisements in the past and are considering more aggressively selling spots in the future, but the main objective is traffic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment with ads but prioritize user experience and traffic goals; evaluate ad opportunities against potential negative impact on engagement and brand voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match tone to vertical and community
rubrics_metrics.description: The A.V. Club has a large, dedicated following... The vertical has its own tone and community and we wanted our emails to reflect that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor voice, content, and frequency to each vertical’s community; do not force a one-size-fits-all voice across distinct audience segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branding/voice constraints when consolidating properties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Onion’s satirical voice can cause some interesting challenges when it comes to sharing or even acknowledging content from other sources... An Onion, Inc. newsletter would be a branding challenge and might require some re-training of our audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When considering a consolidated newsletter across properties, assess brand-voice conflicts and audience expectations; plan for audience re-training and editorial rules for cross-property content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CMS/platform capabilities to enable customization
rubrics_metrics.description: Their CMS-based system didn’t allow for easy viewing of open and click-through rates... we now keep a close eye on those. Mailchimp made it easier to create and house new templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose platforms that provide analytics and flexible templating; leverage platform features to iterate on templates, personalization, and targeting quickly.
